Given the plots of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ above, find ${h}^{′}(-1)$ where $h(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}.$

${h}^{′}(-1)=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The quotient rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)-f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(-1)=\frac{{f}^{′}(-1)\cdot g(-1)-f(-1)\cdot {g}^{′}(-1)}{(g(-1))^{2}}.
$$

From the graphs above, we obtain that $f(-1)=-1$ and $g(-1)=2.$

Additionally:

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (-3,1)$ equals $-1.$ So, ${f}^{′}(-1)=-1.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (-3,1)$ equals $\frac{1}{2}.$ So, ${g}^{′}(-1)=\frac{1}{2}.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(-1) & =\frac{{f}^{′}(-1)\cdot g(-1)-f(-1)\cdot {g}^{′}(-1)}{(g(-1))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot (\frac{1}{2})}{(2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{3}{2}}{4} \\  & =-\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
